<reason>B wins by distinguishing public protection from exclusive purchasing and defending employer financing with subsidized continuity. A established meaningful continuity and administrative-efficiency advantages, but repeatedly attacked full-price COBRA rather than B’s proposed subsidy and answered urgent-access pressure with political accountability. B directly acknowledged limited patient exit while preserving its institutional correction argument. A’s closing dismissed exclusivity instead of explaining why single-payer’s advantages outweighed concentration risk.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B exposed A’s asymmetric treatment of reform: if political action can repair national underfunding, it can also subsidize coverage after job loss. A continued describing employment-related gaps as unavoidable without answering that proposed remedy. This substantially weakened A’s central comparison.</best_rebuttal>
